messages.content: What's the current traffic condition in New York?

function.name: geocode_address
function.description: Transforms a description of a location (like a pair of coordinates, an address, or a name of a place) to a location on the Earth's surface. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

address.description: The address that needs to be geocoded.

locale.description: Preferred locale for the returned address information. (Optional) Default: None

message.content:
I don’t have access to live traffic feeds, so I can’t give you a real‑time snapshot of congestion in New York City right now. However, here’s what you can do to check the current traffic conditions:

| Option | How to Use |
|--------|------------|
| **Google Maps** | Open the app or go to maps.google.com, type “New York City” or your specific address, and tap the “Traffic” layer. |
| **Apple Maps** | On iOS, open Maps, search for “New York City,” then tap the traffic icon (usually a little car). |
| **Waze** | Launch Waze, search for “New York City,” and it will automatically show live traffic, incidents, and suggested routes. |
| **City’s official traffic portal** | NYC’s Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) publishes real‑time traffic camera feeds and incident reports at <https://www1.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/traffic/traffic.shtml>. |
| **Third‑party APIs** | If you’re building an app, you can use services like Google Maps Traffic API, HERE Traffic API, or TomTom Traffic API to pull live traffic data programmatically. |

If you let me know a specific intersection or route, I can describe typical traffic patterns for that area (e.g., peak hours, known bottlenecks).
